template_instructions.content_instructions: Use for adolescents aged 12–15. Address the adolescent directly in clear, age-appropriate language and preserve decision-critical information: purpose, treatment/randomisation where applicable, procedures and duration, main risks/burdens, possible benefit and alternatives, applicable biological samples/genetic testing, basic data confidentiality, contacts and voluntariness. This document records assent; parent/guardian consent is separate and an explicit refusal must be respected. Distinguish required from genuinely optional main-trial activities. Exclude secondary/future use.
template_instructions.styling_instructions: Use clear participant-facing question headings and short sections. Use a clean readable font such as Calibri, Arial, Verdana or Tahoma at about 12 point. Avoid block capitals and unnecessary legalistic text. Use tables or simple flow charts when they improve understanding. Keep the adolescent’s assent record visually distinct from genuinely optional choices. Use Yes/No boxes only for optional activities. Use separate fields for printed name, date and signature.

template_content.section_content: Information for you about a clinical trial Drafting note: Use for ages 12–15. This is assent, not legally effective informed consent. We would like to ask if you want to take part in a clinical trial. Your parent or guardian will also receive information and will be asked for permission because you are under 16. Your own view matters too. Read this information, ask questions and take the time you need. You can say no or change your mind later. A clear refusal or wish to stop must be respected.
template_content.section_style: H2 document subline, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Why is the trial being done and why are you being asked? Explain the condition, purpose, why adolescents are included and why this person may be eligible. State how many people are expected to take part.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What will happen if you take part? Describe the study medicine/intervention, placebo/comparator, randomisation/blinding, screening, visits, tests, duration, responsibilities and what is different from usual care. Explain technical ideas rather than just naming them.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What are the possible benefits? Explain possible personal benefit honestly or state that no direct benefit is expected. Explain that benefit is not guaranteed.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What are the risks and inconveniences? Explain important side effects, unknown risks, pain/discomfort, time burden, reproductive precautions where relevant, privacy risks and what staff will do if there is a problem.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What other treatments are available? Explain the main alternatives and what happens if the adolescent does not take part.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What happens to your samples and genetic information? Explain biological samples used for the main trial: what, how much, why, coding, storage, laboratories/recipients and whether required or optional. [Conditional – genetic/genomic testing] Explain what DNA/genes are, why testing is done, whether required or optional, that DNA is unique, relevant privacy/family risks and whether individual/incidental findings may be returned. Do not include future/secondary research.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What happens to information about you? Explain in understandable language what health/personal information is used, relevant medical-record access, coding, who may see it, security, retention, transfers outside the EEA, rights and who to contact. The parent/guardian form contains the full consent/data-protection details.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: What if something goes wrong, will it cost anything, and how will you hear results? Explain briefly the study-injury/insurance arrangements, any costs or reimbursement that matter to the adolescent, and how overall or relevant individual results will be communicated. The parent/guardian form contains the full details.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Can you say no or stop? Yes. You may say no before the trial starts or ask to stop later without giving a reason. Your usual care will not be taken away. You may also refuse an optional procedure. If a procedure is required for safety or the main trial, the study team will explain whether you can continue without it.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: [Conditional – include only if your participation may continue after you turn 16] What happens when you turn 16? If you turn 16 while the regulated study is still continuing, the study team will give you appropriate information and ask you to provide your own informed consent for continued participation and use of your study data.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text

template_content.section_content: Who can you ask? Provide study doctor/nurse contact details and explain that questions can be asked at any time.
template_content.section_style: H3 module title, Rich body text
